HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS: The patient is a 73-year-old established male with a history of HFrEF (LVEF 25%), CKD Stage 3b, and Type 2 Diabetes who presents today with a 4-day history of progressively worsening dyspnea on exertion, orthopnea requiring 3 pillows at night, and an 8-pound weight gain. PHYSICAL EXAMINATION: Vitals: BP 158/88, HR 96, RR 24, Temp 98.2F, SpO2 91% on room air. General: Mild respiratory distress, speaking in short sentences. Neck: JVD present at 9 cm H2O. Lungs: Crackles appreciated in bilateral bases, extending one-third up. Cardiovascular: Tachycardic, regular rhythm, S3 gallop present, no murmurs. Extremities: 3+ pitting edema bilaterally up to the mid-calf. Warm to touch. DATA REVIEWED: 1. Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (drawn yesterday): BUN 45, Creatinine 2.3 (baseline 1.6), Potassium 5.1. 2. NT-proBNP: 2,850 pg/mL (baseline 600). 3. EKG performed in clinic today: Normal sinus rhythm, rate 95, LVH, no acute ST-T wave changes. ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: 1. Acute decompensated heart failure with reduced ejection fraction. The patient is exhibiting significant volume overload. 2. Acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease Stage 3b, likely cardiorenal etiology given the acute heart failure exacerbation. 3. High Risk Medical Decision Making: We had an extensive discussion regarding the severity of his condition. I recommended direct admission to the hospital for IV diuresis and close monitoring.
